1→# Quiz Engine — Detailed Design
     2→
     3→## File: `src/quiz.ts` (modified)
     4→
     5→## Card Prioritization Algorithm
     6→
     7→The quiz engine selects and orders cards in two tiers:
     8→
     9→### Tier 1: Due Cards
    10→Cards where `nextReviewDate <= today`. Sorted by overdue-ness (most overdue first).
    11→
    12→```ts
    13→function getDueCards(cards: readonly ReviewCard[], today?: string): ReviewCard[] {
    14→  const t = today ?? todayDateString();
    15→  return cards
    16→    .filter(rc => rc.sm2.nextReviewDate <= t)
    17→    .sort((a, b) => {
    18→      // Most overdue first (earlier nextReviewDate = more overdue)
    19→      if (a.sm2.nextReviewDate < b.sm2.nextReviewDate) return -1;
    20→      if (a.sm2.nextReviewDate > b.sm2.nextReviewDate) return 1;
    21→      // Tie-break: lower easiness factor first (harder cards)
    22→      return a.sm2.easinessFactor - b.sm2.easinessFactor;
    23→    });
    24→}
    25→```
    26→
    27→### Tier 2: New Cards
    28→Cards that have never been reviewed (`repetitions === 0` and `interval === 0`). Limited by the daily new-card limit (default: 20).
    29→
    30→```ts
    31→function getNewCards(cards: readonly ReviewCard[], limit: number): ReviewCard[] {
    32→  return cards
    33→    .filter(rc => rc.sm2.repetitions === 0 && rc.sm2.interval === 0)
    34→    .slice(0, limit);
    35→}
    36→```
    37→
    38→### Combined Selection
    39→
    40→```ts
    41→function selectQuizCards(
    42→  cards: readonly ReviewCard[],
    43→  options: { newCardLimit: number; dueOnly: boolean; all: boolean },
    44→  today?: string
    45→): ReviewCard[] {
    46→  if (options.all) {
    47→    return [...cards];  // all cards, no filtering
    48→  }
    49→
    50→  const dueCards = getDueCards(cards, today);
    51→
    52→  if (options.dueOnly) {
    53→    return dueCards;  // only due cards, no new cards
    54→  }
    55→
    56→  const newCards = getNewCards(cards, options.newCardLimit);
    57→  return [...dueCards, ...newCards];  // due first, then new
    58→}
    59→```
    60→
    61→No interleaving: all due cards are presented before any new cards.
    62→
    63→## Daily New-Card Limit
    64→
    65→- Default: 20
    66→- Configurable via `--new-cards <n>` CLI flag
    67→- Set to 0 to disable new cards entirely (equivalent to `--due-only`)
    68→- The limit applies to cards with `repetitions === 0 && interval === 0`
    69→- Note: a card that was reviewed once with "again" has `repetitions=0` but `interval=1` — it is a due card, not a new card. The new-card limit does not apply to it.
    70→
    71→## Updated QuizSession Interface
    72→
    73→```ts
    74→/** Quiz session state for spaced repetition. */
    75→export interface QuizSession {
    76→  readonly cards: readonly ReviewCard[];
    77→  currentIndex: number;
    78→  readonly answers: Map<string, number>;  // cardId -> SM-2 quality grade
    79→  readonly updatedCards: ReviewCard[];     // cards with updated SM-2 state after grading
    80→}
    81→```
    82→
    83→Key changes from current:
    84→- `cards` is `ReviewCard[]` instead of `Card[]`
    85→- `answers` maps to `number` (quality grade 0-5) instead of `boolean`
    86→- `updatedCards` accumulates cards with their new SM-2 state after each answer
    87→
    88→## Updated Function Signatures
    89→
    90→### `startQuiz`
    91→
    92→```ts
    93→/** Start a new quiz session with pre-selected ReviewCards. */
    94→export function startQuiz(cards: ReviewCard[]): QuizSession;
    95→```
    96→
    97→- Initializes session with `currentIndex: 0`, empty `answers` map, empty `updatedCards`
    98→- Card selection/filtering happens before `startQuiz` is called (in CLI layer)
    99→
   100→### `currentCard`
   101→
   102→```ts
   103→/** Get the current ReviewCard, or undefined if quiz is complete. */
   104→export function currentCard(session: QuizSession): ReviewCard | undefined;
   105→```
   106→
   107→### `answerCard`
   108→
   109→```ts
   110→/** Record a graded answer, apply SM-2 update, and advance to next card. */
   111→export function answerCard(session: QuizSession, grade: Grade): void;
   112→```
   113→
   114→**Pseudocode:**
   115→```
   116→function answerCard(session, grade):
   117→  rc = currentCard(session)
   118→  if rc is undefined: return
   119→
   120→  quality = mapGradeToQuality(grade)
   121→  newSM2 = calculateSM2(rc.sm2, quality)
   122→  reviewRecord = { quality, grade, reviewedAt: now(), easinessFactor: newSM2.easinessFactor, interval: newSM2.interval }
   123→
   124→  updatedCard = {
   125→    card: rc.card,
   126→    sm2: newSM2,
   127→    reviewHistory: [...rc.reviewHistory, reviewRecord]
   128→  }
   129→
   130→  session.answers.set(rc.card.id, quality)
   131→  session.updatedCards.push(updatedCard)
   132→  session.currentIndex++
   133→```
   134→
   135→### `isQuizComplete`
   136→
   137→```ts
   138→/** Check if the quiz is complete. */
   139→export function isQuizComplete(session: QuizSession): boolean;
   140→```
   141→
   142→Unchanged logic: `session.currentIndex >= session.cards.length`.
   143→
   144→### `getDueCards` (new export)
   145→
   146→```ts
   147→/** Get cards that are due for review, sorted by overdue-ness. */
   148→export function getDueCards(cards: readonly ReviewCard[], today?: string): ReviewCard[];
   149→```
   150→
   151→### `getNewCards` (new export)
   152→
   153→```ts
   154→/** Get cards that have never been reviewed, up to the specified limit. */
   155→export function getNewCards(cards: readonly ReviewCard[], limit: number): ReviewCard[];
   156→```
   157→
   158→### `selectQuizCards` (new export)
   159→
   160→```ts
   161→/** Select and order cards for a quiz session based on options. */
   162→export function selectQuizCards(
   163→  cards: readonly ReviewCard[],
   164→  options: QuizOptions,
   165→  today?: string
   166→): ReviewCard[];
   167→```
   168→
   169→## QuizOptions Type
   170→
   171→```ts
   172→/** Options for card selection in a quiz session. */
   173→export interface QuizOptions {
   174→  readonly newCardLimit: number;  // default 20
   175→  readonly dueOnly: boolean;     // only show due cards
   176→  readonly all: boolean;         // show all cards regardless of schedule
   177→}
   178→
   179→export const DEFAULT_QUIZ_OPTIONS: QuizOptions = {
   180→  newCardLimit: 20,
   181→  dueOnly: false,
   182→  all: false,
   183→};
   184→```
   185→
   186→## 4-Point Grading Flow
   187→
   188→During a quiz session, for each card:
   189→
   190→1. Display card front (question)
   191→2. User presses Enter to reveal answer
   192→3. Display card back (answer)
   193→4. Prompt: `Rate your recall: (1) Again / (2) Hard / (3) Good / (4) Easy / (q) Quit`
   194→5. User enters `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, or `q`
   195→6. Grade is mapped to SM-2 quality and applied
   196→7. Advance to next card
   197→
   198→The grading prompt accepts single-character input for speed.
   199→
   200→## Session Lifecycle
   201→
   202→```
   203→1. Load deck from file          → ReviewCard[]
   204→2. Select quiz cards            → ReviewCard[] (filtered + sorted)
   205→3. Start quiz session           → QuizSession
   206→4. Loop: show card, grade       → updates QuizSession.updatedCards
   207→5. Quiz complete                → QuizSession with all updatedCards
   208→6. Calculate score              → ScoreSummary
   209→7. Merge updatedCards into deck → full ReviewCard[] with updates applied
   210→8. Save deck to file            → persist to disk
   211→9. Display session summary      → print to console
   212→```
   213→
   214→Step 7 detail: the CLI merges `session.updatedCards` back into the full deck array by matching on `card.id`, then saves the complete deck.
   215→
   216→## Empty State Handling
   217→
   218→| Scenario | Behavior |
   219→|----------|----------|
   220→| Deck file doesn't exist | Print "No deck found. Create cards first." and exit |
   221→| Deck exists but empty | Print "Deck is empty. Add cards first." and exit |
   222→| No due cards and `--due-only` | Print "No cards due for review. Great job!" and exit |
   223→| No due cards and no new cards | Print "No cards due. All caught up!" and exit |
   224→| Some due, some new | Show due cards first, then new cards up to limit |
   225→
   226→## Score Calculation Updates
   227→
   228→`src/score.ts` is updated to accept quality-based answers:
   229→
   230→```ts
   231→/** Calculate score from quality-grade answers. Quality >= 3 counts as correct. */
   232→export function calculateScore(answers: Map<string, number>): ScoreSummary;
   233→```
   234→
   235→The `ScoreSummary` interface remains the same. A quality of 3, 4, or 5 counts as "recalled"; 0, 1, or 2 counts as "incorrect".
   236→
   237→## Testing Strategy
   238→
   239→**Unit tests for card selection:**
   240→- `getDueCards`: returns only cards with nextReviewDate <= today, sorted by overdue-ness
   241→- `getDueCards`: tie-breaking by lower EF (harder cards first)
   242→- `getNewCards`: returns only never-reviewed cards, respects limit
   243→- `selectQuizCards`: `--all` returns all cards
   244→- `selectQuizCards`: `--due-only` excludes new cards
   245→- `selectQuizCards`: default returns due + new (up to limit), due first
   246→
   247→**Unit tests for session lifecycle:**
   248→- `startQuiz`: initializes with correct defaults
   249→- `answerCard`: applies SM-2 calculation and pushes to updatedCards
   250→- `answerCard`: records correct quality in answers map
   251→- `isQuizComplete`: true when currentIndex >= cards.length
   252→- `currentCard`: returns undefined when quiz complete
   253→
   254→**Integration test scenarios:**
   255→- Full flow: load -> filter -> quiz all cards -> verify SM2 states updated correctly
   256→- Mixed grades: verify each grade produces expected SM2 state changes
   257→- Card with "again" grade reviewed again appears as due card (not new card)
   258→

1→# Architecture Overview — Spaced Repetition
     2→
     3→## Subsystem Map
     4→
     5→```
     6→src/
     7→  sm2.ts       — SM-2 algorithm core (pure functions, no I/O)
     8→  storage.ts   — JSON file persistence for decks with review data
     9→  quiz.ts      — Quiz engine with card prioritization and graded answers (modified)
    10→  score.ts     — Score calculation updated for quality-based grading (modified)
    11→  card.ts      — Card interface (unchanged)
    12→  index.ts     — CLI entry point with new flags and interactive prompts (modified)
    13→tests/
    14→  sm2.test.ts      — SM-2 algorithm tests
    15→  storage.test.ts  — Storage layer tests
    16→  quiz.test.ts     — Quiz engine tests
    17→  score.test.ts    — Score calculation tests
    18→```
    19→
    20→## Subsystem Responsibilities
    21→
    22→### 1. SM-2 Algorithm Core (`src/sm2.ts`) — NEW
    23→- Pure, stateless functions implementing the SM-2 algorithm
    24→- `createInitialSM2State()` — returns default state (EF=2.5, repetitions=0, interval=0)
    25→- `calculateSM2(state, quality)` — takes current state + grade (0-5), returns new state
    26→- `mapGradeToQuality(grade)` — maps 4-point user grade (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) to SM-2 quality (0/3/4/5)
    27→- `isDue(state, now)` — checks if a card is due for review
    28→- No dependencies on other modules; no I/O; fully testable in isolation
    29→
    30→### 2. Storage Layer (`src/storage.ts`) — NEW
    31→- Reads and writes deck JSON files containing cards with embedded SM-2 state
    32→- `loadDeck(filePath)` — reads JSON file, returns array of ReviewCards; handles missing files (returns empty)
    33→- `saveDeck(filePath, cards)` — writes ReviewCard array to JSON file (atomic write with .bak backup)
    34→- Backward compatible: cards without SM-2 fields are assigned default initial state on load
    35→- Versioned migration pipeline for schema evolution
    36→- Load-time validation of required fields and data types
    37→- Uses `Bun.file()` and `Bun.write()` for I/O
    38→
    39→### 3. Quiz Engine (`src/quiz.ts`) — MODIFIED
    40→- Card selection: filters due cards and new cards separately
    41→- Prioritization: due cards sorted by overdue-ness (most overdue first), then new cards up to daily limit
    42→- Answer recording changes from `boolean` to quality grade (`number`)
    43→- After each answer, applies SM-2 calculation and updates card state
    44→- Session tracks `ReviewCard[]` instead of `Card[]`
    45→
    46→### 4. Score Calculation (`src/score.ts`) — MODIFIED
    47→- Updated to work with quality grades instead of boolean correct/incorrect
    48→- Correct = quality >= 3 (maps to SM-2 "successful recall")
    49→- Adds session summary with next review date information
    50→
    51→### 5. CLI Integration (`src/index.ts`) — MODIFIED
    52→- Parses new flags: `--due-only`, `--new-cards <n>`, `--all`, `--help`
    53→- Interactive grading prompt: shows 4 options (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) after revealing answer
    54→- Graceful quit ('q' key) and SIGINT handler to save partial progress
    55→- Session summary output: cards reviewed, accuracy, next review dates
    56→- Auto-saves review results to deck file after quiz completes
    57→
    58→## Boundaries and Communication
    59→
    60→```
    61→CLI (index.ts)
    62→  │
    63→  ├── reads flags, orchestrates session lifecycle
    64→  │
    65→  ├──▶ Storage (storage.ts)
    66→  │      │  loadDeck() → ReviewCard[]
    67→  │      │  saveDeck(ReviewCard[])
    68→  │      │
    69→  │      └──▶ SM2 Core (sm2.ts)
    70→  │             createInitialSM2State() — used for backward compat
    71→  │
    72→  ├──▶ Quiz Engine (quiz.ts)
    73→  │      │  getDueCards(), getNewCards()
    74→  │      │  startQuiz(), answerCard(), currentCard()
    75→  │      │
    76→  │      └──▶ SM2 Core (sm2.ts)
    77→  │             calculateSM2() — called after each answer
    78→  │             mapGradeToQuality() — 4-point → SM-2 mapping
    79→  │
    80→  └──▶ Score (score.ts)
    81→         calculateScore(), formatScore()
    82→```
    83→
    84→## Data Flow
    85→
    86→1. **Load**: CLI calls `loadDeck()` which reads JSON and hydrates `ReviewCard[]`
    87→2. **Filter**: Quiz engine separates due cards from new cards, applies limits
    88→3. **Quiz loop**: For each card — show front, reveal back, prompt for grade
    89→4. **Update**: After each grade, `calculateSM2()` produces new SM2State; card is updated in-memory
    90→5. **Save**: After quiz completes, CLI calls `saveDeck()` to persist all updated states
    91→6. **Report**: Score module summarizes the session
    92→
    93→## Key Design Decisions
    94→
    95→- **SM-2 state per card (not per direction)**: Each card has one SM2State. No front/back separate tracking.
    96→- **4-point grading scale**: Again (0) / Hard (3) / Good (4) / Easy (5) mapped to SM-2 quality. Balances simplicity with expressiveness.
    97→- **Embedded SM-2 fields**: SM-2 state is stored alongside card data in the same JSON file, not in a separate database.
    98→- **No external dependencies**: SM-2 is simple math; dates use built-in `Date`; I/O uses Bun APIs.
    99→- **Dates as ISO 8601 strings**: `nextReviewDate` uses date-only format (`YYYY-MM-DD`) to avoid timezone issues.
   100→- **Composition over extension**: `ReviewCard` wraps `Card` + `SM2State` + `ReviewRecord[]` rather than adding optional fields to `Card`.
   101→

1→# Conventions
     2→
     3→## Language & Runtime
     4→- TypeScript with strict mode enabled
     5→- Bun as the runtime and build tool (not Node.js)
     6→- ESNext target and module system with bundler module resolution
     7→
     8→## Project Structure
     9→```
    10→src/           # Source modules (one concept per file)
    11→  index.ts     # CLI entry point
    12→  card.ts      # Card data model and creation
    13→  quiz.ts      # Quiz session logic
    14→  score.ts     # Score calculation and formatting
    15→tests/         # Test files mirroring src/ with .test.ts suffix
    16→dist/          # Build output (bun build)
    17→```
    18→
    19→## Code Style
    20→- Linting and formatting via Biome (recommended rules, organized imports)
    21→- `.goodplan/` directory is excluded from Biome checks
    22→- ES module syntax (`import`/`export`), no CommonJS
    23→- `type` imports used for type-only imports (e.g., `import type { Card }`)
    24→
    25→## Naming
    26→- Interfaces: PascalCase (e.g., `Card`, `QuizSession`, `ScoreSummary`)
    27→- Functions: camelCase, exported as named exports (e.g., `createCard`, `startQuiz`)
    28→- Files: lowercase, single-word names matching the primary concept they contain
    29→- No default exports -- all exports are named
    30→
    31→## Type Patterns
    32→- Interfaces prefer `readonly` properties where mutation is not needed
    33→- `readonly` arrays used for immutable collections (e.g., `readonly string[]`, `readonly Card[]`)
    34→- Mutable state is explicit (e.g., `currentIndex` in `QuizSession`)
    35→
    36→## Documentation
    37→- JSDoc single-line comments (`/** ... */`) on all exported interfaces and functions
    38→- No inline comments except for TODOs or clarifying notes
    39→
    40→## Testing
    41→- Bun's built-in test runner (`bun:test`)
    42→- Test files in `tests/` directory with `.test.ts` suffix
    43→- Tests use `describe`/`it`/`expect` pattern
    44→- Test file names mirror source file names (e.g., `card.test.ts` tests `card.ts`)
    45→
    46→## Build & Scripts
    47→- `bun build src/index.ts --outdir dist` for production build
    48→- `biome check .` for linting
    49→- `bun test` for running tests
    50→

1→# SM-2 Algorithm Core — Detailed Design
     2→
     3→## File: `src/sm2.ts`
     4→
     5→## Types
     6→
     7→```ts
     8→/** SM-2 quality grade: integer 0-5 for compile-time safety. */
     9→export type SM2Quality = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5;
    10→
    11→/** SM-2 state tracked per card. */
    12→export interface SM2State {
    13→  readonly easinessFactor: number;   // >= 1.3, default 2.5
    14→  readonly repetitions: number;      // consecutive correct count, resets on failure
    15→  readonly interval: number;         // days until next review
    16→  readonly nextReviewDate: string;   // ISO 8601 date-only string (YYYY-MM-DD)
    17→}
    18→
    19→/** Record of a single review event. */
    20→export interface ReviewRecord {
    21→  readonly quality: SM2Quality;      // SM-2 quality grade (0-5) that was applied
    22→  readonly grade: Grade;             // user-facing grade that was given
    23→  readonly reviewedAt: string;       // ISO 8601 datetime string
    24→  readonly easinessFactor: number;   // EF after this review
    25→  readonly interval: number;         // interval after this review
    26→}
    27→
    28→/** 4-point user-facing grade scale. */
    29→export type Grade = "again" | "hard" | "good" | "easy";
    30→```
    31→
    32→## Constants
    33→
    34→```ts
    35→const INITIAL_EASINESS_FACTOR = 2.5;
    36→const MINIMUM_EASINESS_FACTOR = 1.3;
    37→const INITIAL_REPETITIONS = 0;
    38→const INITIAL_INTERVAL = 0;
    39→
    40→/** Mapping from user-facing grade to SM-2 quality (0-5). */
    41→const GRADE_TO_QUALITY: Record<Grade, SM2Quality> = {
    42→  again: 0,  // complete failure — resets repetitions
    43→  hard: 3,   // correct but with serious difficulty
    44→  good: 4,   // correct with some hesitation
    45→  easy: 5,   // perfect recall
    46→};
    47→```
    48→
    49→## Function Signatures
    50→
    51→### `createInitialSM2State`
    52→
    53→```ts
    54→/** Create the default SM-2 state for a new card. */
    55→export function createInitialSM2State(today?: string): SM2State;
    56→```
    57→
    58→- Returns `{ easinessFactor: 2.5, repetitions: 0, interval: 0, nextReviewDate: today }`
    59→- `today` defaults to current date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format if not provided
    60→- A card with initial state is immediately due for review
    61→
    62→### `calculateSM2`
    63→
    64→```ts
    65→/** Apply one review to an SM-2 state, returning the updated state. Pure function. */
    66→export function calculateSM2(state: SM2State, quality: SM2Quality, today?: string): SM2State;
    67→```
    68→
    69→- `quality` must be an integer 0-5 (validated; throws if out of range)
    70→- `today` defaults to current date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format
    71→
    72→**Algorithm pseudocode:**
    73→
    74→```
    75→function calculateSM2(state, quality, today):
    76→  // Step 1: Determine interval and repetitions (using CURRENT EF)
    77→  if quality >= 3:
    78→    if state.repetitions === 0:
    79→      newInterval = 1
    80→    else if state.repetitions === 1:
    81→      newInterval = 6
    82→    else:
    83→      newInterval = round(state.interval * state.easinessFactor)
    84→    newInterval = max(newInterval, 1)   // safety guard
    85→    newRepetitions = state.repetitions + 1
    86→  else:
    87→    // Failed recall — reset
    88→    newInterval = 1
    89→    newRepetitions = 0
    90→
    91→  // Step 2: Update easiness factor (AFTER interval calculation)
    92→  newEF = state.easinessFactor + (0.1 - (5 - quality) * (0.08 + (5 - quality) * 0.02))
    93→  newEF = max(newEF, 1.3)
    94→
    95→  // Step 3: Calculate next review date
    96→  nextReviewDate = addDays(today, newInterval)
    97→
    98→  return { easinessFactor: newEF, repetitions: newRepetitions, interval: newInterval, nextReviewDate }
    99→```
   100→
   101→### `mapGradeToQuality`
   102→
   103→```ts
   104→/** Map a user-facing grade to an SM-2 quality value (0-5). */
   105→export function mapGradeToQuality(grade: Grade): SM2Quality;
   106→```
   107→
   108→- `"again"` -> 0
   109→- `"hard"` -> 3
   110→- `"good"` -> 4
   111→- `"easy"` -> 5
   112→
   113→### `isDue`
   114→
   115→```ts
   116→/** Check if a card is due for review on or before the given date. */
   117→export function isDue(state: SM2State, today?: string): boolean;
   118→```
   119→
   120→- Returns `true` if `state.nextReviewDate <= today` (string comparison works for YYYY-MM-DD)
   121→- `today` defaults to current date
   122→
   123→### `getOverdueDays`
   124→
   125→```ts
   126→/** Calculate how many days overdue a card is. Returns 0 if not overdue. */
   127→export function getOverdueDays(state: SM2State, today?: string): number;
   128→```
   129→
   130→- Used by quiz engine for sorting by overdue-ness
   131→
   132→### Helper: `todayDateString`
   133→
   134→```ts
   135→/** Get today's date as a YYYY-MM-DD string. */
   136→export function todayDateString(): string;
   137→```
   138→
   139→### Helper: `addDays`
   140→
   141→```ts
   142→/** Add N days to a YYYY-MM-DD date string, return new YYYY-MM-DD string. */
   143→function addDays(dateStr: string, days: number): string;
   144→```
   145→
   146→- Internal helper, not exported
   147→- Uses `new Date()` arithmetic
   148→
   149→## Grade Mapping Rationale
   150→
   151→The full SM-2 scale (0-5) has 6 options which is too many for a CLI prompt. The 4-point scale provides a good balance between simplicity and expressiveness:
   152→
   153→| User Grade | SM-2 Quality | Meaning | SM-2 Effect |
   154→|-----------|-------------|---------|-------------|
   155→| Again (1) | 0 | No recall / wrong | Reset repetitions to 0, interval to 1 day |
   156→| Hard (2) | 3 | Recalled with difficulty | Increment repetitions, EF decreases |
   157→| Good (3) | 4 | Correct with some hesitation | Increment repetitions, EF stays ~same |
   158→| Easy (4) | 5 | Perfect recall | Increment repetitions, EF increases |
   159→
   160→Key bindings use `1/2/3/4` for speed and intuitiveness (worst to best).
   161→
   162→## Edge Cases
   163→
   164→1. **Quality validation**: `calculateSM2` throws `RangeError` if quality is not an integer 0-5
   165→2. **EF floor**: Easiness factor never drops below 1.3, even with repeated "again" grades
   166→3. **First review**: When `repetitions === 0` and quality >= 3, interval becomes 1 day (not 0)
   167→4. **Interval rounding**: `Math.round()` is used for interval calculation (SM-2 spec)
   168→5. **Date-only strings**: All dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` — no time component, no timezone ambiguity
   169→6. **Negative interval**: Not possible given the algorithm, but `Math.max(newInterval, 1)` as a safety guard
   170→
   171→## EF Progression Examples
   172→
   173→Starting from EF=2.5:
   174→- After quality=5: EF = 2.5 + 0.1 = 2.6
   175→- After quality=3: EF = 2.5 + 0.1 - 0.16 - 0.08 = 2.36
   176→- After quality=0: EF = 2.5 + 0.1 - 0.4 - 0.5 = 1.7
   177→- After quality=0 again from 1.7: EF = 1.7 + 0.1 - 0.4 - 0.5 = 0.9 → clamped to 1.3
   178→
   179→## Interval Progression (all Easy, EF=2.5)
   180→
   181→| Review # | Repetitions | Interval | Next Review |
   182→|----------|------------|----------|-------------|
   183→| 1st | 0 → 1 | 1 day | tomorrow |
   184→| 2nd | 1 → 2 | 6 days | +6 days |
   185→| 3rd | 2 → 3 | round(6 * 2.5) = 15 days | +15 days |
   186→| 4th | 3 → 4 | round(15 * 2.6) = 39 days | +39 days |
   187→
   188→## Testing Strategy
   189→
   190→All SM-2 functions are pure (no I/O, no side effects), making them ideal for unit testing.
   191→
   192→**Key test cases for `calculateSM2`:**
   193→- Quality >= 3 with repetitions=0 produces interval=1
   194→- Quality >= 3 with repetitions=1 produces interval=6
   195→- Quality >= 3 with repetitions>=2 uses `interval * oldEF` (verify old EF is used, not new)
   196→- Quality < 3 resets repetitions to 0 and interval to 1
   197→- EF never drops below 1.3 (test with repeated low-quality grades)
   198→- EF increases with quality=5, decreases with quality=3, stays roughly same with quality=4
   199→- Interval is always >= 1 (safety guard)
   200→
   201→**Key test cases for `mapGradeToQuality`:**
   202→- Each grade maps to the expected quality value
   203→- Return type is `SM2Quality`
   204→
   205→**Key test cases for `isDue` / `getOverdueDays`:**
   206→- Card due today returns true / 0 days overdue
   207→- Card due yesterday returns true / 1 day overdue
   208→- Card due tomorrow returns false / 0 days overdue
   209→
   210→**Key test cases for `createInitialSM2State`:**
   211→- Default values: EF=2.5, repetitions=0, interval=0
   212→- nextReviewDate matches provided or current date
   213→

1→# Quiz Engine — Detailed Design
     2→
     3→## File: `src/quiz.ts` (modified)
     4→
     5→## Card Prioritization Algorithm
     6→
     7→The quiz engine selects and orders cards in two tiers:
     8→
     9→### Tier 1: Due Cards
    10→Cards where `nextReviewDate <= today`. Sorted by overdue-ness (most overdue first).
    11→
    12→```ts
    13→function getDueCards(cards: readonly ReviewCard[], today?: string): ReviewCard[] {
    14→  const t = today ?? todayDateString();
    15→  return cards
    16→    .filter(rc => rc.sm2.nextReviewDate <= t)
    17→    .sort((a, b) => {
    18→      // Most overdue first (earlier nextReviewDate = more overdue)
    19→      if (a.sm2.nextReviewDate < b.sm2.nextReviewDate) return -1;
    20→      if (a.sm2.nextReviewDate > b.sm2.nextReviewDate) return 1;
    21→      // Tie-break: lower easiness factor first (harder cards)
    22→      return a.sm2.easinessFactor - b.sm2.easinessFactor;
    23→    });
    24→}
    25→```
    26→
    27→### Tier 2: New Cards
    28→Cards that have never been reviewed (`repetitions === 0` and `interval === 0`). Limited by the daily new-card limit (default: 20).
    29→
    30→```ts
    31→function getNewCards(cards: readonly ReviewCard[], limit: number): ReviewCard[] {
    32→  return cards
    33→    .filter(rc => rc.sm2.repetitions === 0 && rc.sm2.interval === 0)
    34→    .slice(0, limit);
    35→}
    36→```
    37→
    38→### Combined Selection
    39→
    40→```ts
    41→function selectQuizCards(
    42→  cards: readonly ReviewCard[],
    43→  options: { newCardLimit: number; dueOnly: boolean; all: boolean },
    44→  today?: string
    45→): ReviewCard[] {
    46→  if (options.all) {
    47→    return [...cards];  // all cards, no filtering
    48→  }
    49→
    50→  const dueCards = getDueCards(cards, today);
    51→
    52→  if (options.dueOnly) {
    53→    return dueCards;  // only due cards, no new cards
    54→  }
    55→
    56→  const newCards = getNewCards(cards, options.newCardLimit);
    57→  return [...dueCards, ...newCards];  // due first, then new
    58→}
    59→```
    60→
    61→No interleaving: all due cards are presented before any new cards.
    62→
    63→## Daily New-Card Limit
    64→
    65→- Default: 20
    66→- Configurable via `--new-cards <n>` CLI flag
    67→- Set to 0 to disable new cards entirely (equivalent to `--due-only`)
    68→- The limit applies to cards with `repetitions === 0 && interval === 0`
    69→- Note: a card that was reviewed once with "again" has `repetitions=0` but `interval=1` — it is a due card, not a new card. The new-card limit does not apply to it.
    70→
    71→## Updated QuizSession Interface
    72→
    73→```ts
    74→/** Quiz session state for spaced repetition. */
    75→export interface QuizSession {
    76→  readonly cards: readonly ReviewCard[];
    77→  currentIndex: number;
    78→  readonly answers: Map<string, number>;  // cardId -> SM-2 quality grade
    79→  readonly updatedCards: ReviewCard[];     // cards with updated SM-2 state after grading
    80→}
    81→```
    82→
    83→Key changes from current:
    84→- `cards` is `ReviewCard[]` instead of `Card[]`
    85→- `answers` maps to `number` (quality grade 0-5) instead of `boolean`
    86→- `updatedCards` accumulates cards with their new SM-2 state after each answer
    87→
    88→## Updated Function Signatures
    89→
    90→### `startQuiz`
    91→
    92→```ts
    93→/** Start a new quiz session with pre-selected ReviewCards. */
    94→export function startQuiz(cards: ReviewCard[]): QuizSession;
    95→```
    96→
    97→- Initializes session with `currentIndex: 0`, empty `answers` map, empty `updatedCards`
    98→- Card selection/filtering happens before `startQuiz` is called (in CLI layer)
    99→
   100→### `currentCard`
   101→
   102→```ts
   103→/** Get the current ReviewCard, or undefined if quiz is complete. */
   104→export function currentCard(session: QuizSession): ReviewCard | undefined;
   105→```
   106→
   107→### `answerCard`
   108→
   109→```ts
   110→/** Record a graded answer, apply SM-2 update, and advance to next card. */
   111→export function answerCard(session: QuizSession, grade: Grade): void;
   112→```
   113→
   114→**Pseudocode:**
   115→```
   116→function answerCard(session, grade):
   117→  rc = currentCard(session)
   118→  if rc is undefined: return
   119→
   120→  quality = mapGradeToQuality(grade)
   121→  newSM2 = calculateSM2(rc.sm2, quality)
   122→  reviewRecord = { quality, grade, reviewedAt: now(), easinessFactor: newSM2.easinessFactor, interval: newSM2.interval }
   123→
   124→  updatedCard = {
   125→    card: rc.card,
   126→    sm2: newSM2,
   127→    reviewHistory: [...rc.reviewHistory, reviewRecord]
   128→  }
   129→
   130→  session.answers.set(rc.card.id, quality)
   131→  session.updatedCards.push(updatedCard)
   132→  session.currentIndex++
   133→```
   134→
   135→### `isQuizComplete`
   136→
   137→```ts
   138→/** Check if the quiz is complete. */
   139→export function isQuizComplete(session: QuizSession): boolean;
   140→```
   141→
   142→Unchanged logic: `session.currentIndex >= session.cards.length`.
   143→
   144→### `getDueCards` (new export)
   145→
   146→```ts
   147→/** Get cards that are due for review, sorted by overdue-ness. */
   148→export function getDueCards(cards: readonly ReviewCard[], today?: string): ReviewCard[];
   149→```
   150→
   151→### `getNewCards` (new export)
   152→
   153→```ts
   154→/** Get cards that have never been reviewed, up to the specified limit. */
   155→export function getNewCards(cards: readonly ReviewCard[], limit: number): ReviewCard[];
   156→```
   157→
   158→### `selectQuizCards` (new export)
   159→
   160→```ts
   161→/** Select and order cards for a quiz session based on options. */
   162→export function selectQuizCards(
   163→  cards: readonly ReviewCard[],
   164→  options: QuizOptions,
   165→  today?: string
   166→): ReviewCard[];
   167→```
   168→
   169→## QuizOptions Type
   170→
   171→```ts
   172→/** Options for card selection in a quiz session. */
   173→export interface QuizOptions {
   174→  readonly newCardLimit: number;  // default 20
   175→  readonly dueOnly: boolean;     // only show due cards
   176→  readonly all: boolean;         // show all cards regardless of schedule
   177→}
   178→
   179→export const DEFAULT_QUIZ_OPTIONS: QuizOptions = {
   180→  newCardLimit: 20,
   181→  dueOnly: false,
   182→  all: false,
   183→};
   184→```
   185→
   186→## 4-Point Grading Flow
   187→
   188→During a quiz session, for each card:
   189→
   190→1. Display card front (question)
   191→2. User presses Enter to reveal answer
   192→3. Display card back (answer)
   193→4. Prompt: `Rate your recall: (1) Again / (2) Hard / (3) Good / (4) Easy / (q) Quit`
   194→5. User enters `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, or `q`
   195→6. Grade is mapped to SM-2 quality and applied
   196→7. Advance to next card
   197→
   198→The grading prompt accepts single-character input for speed.
   199→
   200→## Session Lifecycle
   201→
   202→```
   203→1. Load deck from file          → ReviewCard[]
   204→2. Select quiz cards            → ReviewCard[] (filtered + sorted)
   205→3. Start quiz session           → QuizSession
   206→4. Loop: show card, grade       → updates QuizSession.updatedCards
   207→5. Quiz complete                → QuizSession with all updatedCards
   208→6. Calculate score              → ScoreSummary
   209→7. Merge updatedCards into deck → full ReviewCard[] with updates applied
   210→8. Save deck to file            → persist to disk
   211→9. Display session summary      → print to console
   212→```
   213→
   214→Step 7 detail: the CLI merges `session.updatedCards` back into the full deck array by matching on `card.id`, then saves the complete deck.
   215→
   216→## Empty State Handling
   217→
   218→| Scenario | Behavior |
   219→|----------|----------|
   220→| Deck file doesn't exist | Print "No deck found. Create cards first." and exit |
   221→| Deck exists but empty | Print "Deck is empty. Add cards first." and exit |
   222→| No due cards and `--due-only` | Print "No cards due for review. Great job!" and exit |
   223→| No due cards and no new cards | Print "No cards due. All caught up!" and exit |
   224→| Some due, some new | Show due cards first, then new cards up to limit |
   225→
   226→## Score Calculation Updates
   227→
   228→`src/score.ts` is updated to accept quality-based answers:
   229→
   230→```ts
   231→/** Calculate score from quality-grade answers. Quality >= 3 counts as correct. */
   232→export function calculateScore(answers: Map<string, number>): ScoreSummary;
   233→```
   234→
   235→The `ScoreSummary` interface remains the same. A quality of 3, 4, or 5 counts as "recalled"; 0, 1, or 2 counts as "incorrect".
   236→
   237→## Testing Strategy
   238→
   239→**Unit tests for card selection:**
   240→- `getDueCards`: returns only cards with nextReviewDate <= today, sorted by overdue-ness
   241→- `getDueCards`: tie-breaking by lower EF (harder cards first)
   242→- `getNewCards`: returns only never-reviewed cards, respects limit
   243→- `selectQuizCards`: `--all` returns all cards
   244→- `selectQuizCards`: `--due-only` excludes new cards
   245→- `selectQuizCards`: default returns due + new (up to limit), due first
   246→
   247→**Unit tests for session lifecycle:**
   248→- `startQuiz`: initializes with correct defaults
   249→- `answerCard`: applies SM-2 calculation and pushes to updatedCards
   250→- `answerCard`: records correct quality in answers map
   251→- `isQuizComplete`: true when currentIndex >= cards.length
   252→- `currentCard`: returns undefined when quiz complete
   253→
   254→**Integration test scenarios:**
   255→- Full flow: load -> filter -> quiz all cards -> verify SM2 states updated correctly
   256→- Mixed grades: verify each grade produces expected SM2 state changes
   257→- Card with "again" grade reviewed again appears as due card (not new card)
   258→

    22→### 1. SM-2 Algorithm Core (`src/sm2.ts`) — NEW
    23→- Pure, stateless functions implementing the SM-2 algorithm
    24→- `createInitialSM2State()` — returns default state (EF=2.5, repetitions=0, interval=0)
    25→- `calculateSM2(state, quality)` — takes current state + grade (0-5), returns new state
    26→- `mapGradeToQuality(grade)` — maps 4-point user grade (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) to SM-2 quality (0/3/4/5)
    27→- `isDue(state, now)` — checks if a card is due for review
    28→- No dependencies on other modules; no I/O; fully testable in isolation
    29→
    30→### 2. Storage Layer (`src/storage.ts`) — NEW
    31→- Reads and writes deck JSON files containing cards with embedded SM-2 state
    32→- `loadDeck(filePath)` — reads JSON file, returns array of ReviewCards; handles missing files (returns empty)
    33→- `saveDeck(filePath, cards)` — writes ReviewCard array to JSON file (atomic write with .bak backup)
    34→- Backward compatible: cards without SM-2 fields are assigned default initial state on load
    35→- Versioned migration pipeline for schema evolution
    36→- Load-time validation of required fields and data types
    37→- Uses `Bun.file()` and `Bun.write()` for I/O
    38→
    39→### 3. Quiz Engine (`src/quiz.ts`) — MODIFIED
    40→- Card selection: filters due cards and new cards separately
    41→- Prioritization: due cards sorted by overdue-ness (most overdue first), then new cards up to daily limit
    42→- Answer recording changes from `boolean` to quality grade (`number`)
    43→- After each answer, applies SM-2 calculation and updates card state
    44→- Session tracks `ReviewCard[]` instead of `Card[]`
    45→
    46→### 4. Score Calculation (`src/score.ts`) — MODIFIED
    47→- Updated to work with quality grades instead of boolean correct/incorrect
    48→- Correct = quality >= 3 (maps to SM-2 "successful recall")
    49→- Adds session summary with next review date information
    50→
    51→### 5. CLI Integration (`src/index.ts`) — MODIFIED
    52→- Parses new flags: `--due-only`, `--new-cards <n>`, `--all`, `--help`
    53→- Interactive grading prompt: shows 4 options (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) after revealing answer
    54→- Graceful quit ('q' key) and SIGINT handler to save partial progress
    55→- Session summary output: cards reviewed, accuracy, next review dates
    56→- Auto-saves review results to deck file after quiz completes
    57→
    58→## Boundaries and Communication
    59→
    60→```
    61→CLI (index.ts)
    62→  │
    63→  ├── reads flags, orchestrates session lifecycle
    64→  │
    65→  ├──▶ Storage (storage.ts)
    66→  │      │  loadDeck() → ReviewCard[]
    67→  │      │  saveDeck(ReviewCard[])
    68→  │      │
    69→  │      └──▶ SM2 Core (sm2.ts)
    70→  │             createInitialSM2State() — used for backward compat
    71→  │
    72→  ├──▶ Quiz Engine (quiz.ts)
    73→  │      │  getDueCards(), getNewCards()
    74→  │      │  startQuiz(), answerCard(), currentCard()
    75→  │      │
    76→  │      └──▶ SM2 Core (sm2.ts)
    77→  │             calculateSM2() — called after each answer
    78→  │             mapGradeToQuality() — 4-point → SM-2 mapping
    79→  │
    80→  └──▶ Score (score.ts)
    81→         calculateScore(), formatScore()
    82→```
    83→
    84→## Data Flow
    85→
    86→1. **Load**: CLI calls `loadDeck()` which reads JSON and hydrates `ReviewCard[]`
    87→2. **Filter**: Quiz engine separates due cards from new cards, applies limits
    88→3. **Quiz loop**: For each card — show front, reveal back, prompt for grade
    89→4. **Update**: After each grade, `calculateSM2()` produces new SM2State; card is updated in-memory
    90→5. **Save**: After quiz completes, CLI calls `saveDeck()` to persist all updated states
    91→6. **Report**: Score module summarizes the session
    92→
    93→## Key Design Decisions
    94→
    95→- **SM-2 state per card (not per direction)**: Each card has one SM2State. No front/back separate tracking.
    96→- **4-point grading scale**: Again (0) / Hard (3) / Good (4) / Easy (5) mapped to SM-2 quality. Balances simplicity with expressiveness.
    97→- **Embedded SM-2 fields**: SM-2 state is stored alongside card data in the same JSON file, not in a separate database.
    98→- **No external dependencies**: SM-2 is simple math; dates use built-in `Date`; I/O uses Bun APIs.
    99→- **Dates as ISO 8601 strings**: `nextReviewDate` uses date-only format (`YYYY-MM-DD`) to avoid timezone issues.
   100→- **Composition over extension**: `ReviewCard` wraps `Card` + `SM2State` + `ReviewRecord[]` rather than adding optional fields to `Card`.
   101→

     5→## JSON File Format

    63→
    64→## Schema Description
    65→
    66→### Root Object
    67→| Field | Type | Description |
    68→|-------|------|-------------|
    69→| `version` | `number` | Schema version for future migrations. Currently `1`. |
    70→| `cards` | `ReviewCard[]` | Array of cards with their SM-2 state and review history. |
    71→
    72→### ReviewCard (each entry in `cards`)
    73→| Field | Type | Description |
    74→|-------|------|-------------|
    75→| `card` | `Card` | The base card data (id, front, back, tags, createdAt). |
    76→| `sm2` | `SM2State` | Current SM-2 algorithm state. |
    77→| `reviewHistory` | `ReviewRecord[]` | Chronological list of all past reviews. |
    78→
    79→## Backward Compatibility
    80→
    81→When loading a file that contains plain `Card` objects (no `sm2` or `reviewHistory` fields), the storage layer treats them as new cards:
    82→
    83→```ts
    84→// During load, if a card entry lacks sm2 data:
    85→if (!entry.sm2) {
    86→  return {
    87→    card: entry.card ?? entry,  // handle both wrapped and flat card formats
    88→    sm2: createInitialSM2State(),
    89→    reviewHistory: [],
    90→  };
    91→}
    92→```
    93→
    94→This means existing deck files created before spaced repetition was added will work without manual migration. The SM-2 fields are populated with defaults on first load and persisted on next save.
    95→
    96→### Version Migration Pipeline
    97→
    98→Migrations are defined as a chain of transforms, each upgrading from version N to N+1:
    99→
   100→```ts
   101→type Migration = (data: unknown) => unknown;
   102→
   103→const MIGRATIONS: Record<number, Migration> = {
   104→  0: migrateV0toV1,  // flat Card[] → { version: 1, cards: ReviewCard[] }
   105→  // Future: 1: migrateV1toV2,
   106→};
   107→
   108→function runMigrations(data: unknown): DeckFile {
   109→  let version = (data as any)?.version ?? 0;
   110→  let current = data;
   111→
   112→  while (version < CURRENT_DECK_VERSION) {
   113→    const migrate = MIGRATIONS[version];
   114→    if (!migrate) {
   115→      throw new Error(`No migration path from version ${version} to ${CURRENT_DECK_VERSION}`);
   116→    }
   117→    current = migrate(current);
   118→    version++;
   119→  }
   120→
   121→  if (version > CURRENT_DECK_VERSION) {
   122→    throw new Error(
   123→      `Deck file version ${version} is newer than supported version ${CURRENT_DECK_VERSION}. Please update the CLI.`
   124→    );
   125→  }
   126→
   127→  return current as DeckFile;
   128→}
   129→```
   130→
   131→- If `version` is missing, treat as version 0 (pre-SM2 format)
   132→- Version 0: flat array of `Card` objects -> wrap each in `ReviewCard` with default SM2State
   133→- Version 1: current format with `ReviewCard` objects
   134→- Forward-version guard: throws if file version exceeds `CURRENT_DECK_VERSION`
   135→
   136→### Load Validation
   137→
   138→After migration, loaded data is validated before use:
   139→
   140→```ts
   141→function validateDeck(data: DeckFile): void {
   142→  if (!Array.isArray(data.cards)) {
   143→    throw new Error("Invalid deck file: 'cards' must be an array");
   144→  }
   145→  for (const rc of data.cards) {
   146→    if (!rc.card?.id || typeof rc.card.id !== "string") {
   147→      throw new Error("Invalid card: missing or non-string 'id'");
   148→    }
   149→    if (typeof rc.card.front !== "string" || typeof rc.card.back !== "string") {
   150→      throw new Error(`Invalid card ${rc.card.id}: 'front' and 'back' must be strings`);
   151→    }
   152→    if (typeof rc.sm2?.easinessFactor !== "number" || isNaN(rc.sm2.easinessFactor)) {
   153→      throw new Error(`Invalid SM2 state for card ${rc.card.id}: bad easinessFactor`);
   154→    }
   155→    if (typeof rc.sm2?.nextReviewDate !== "string" || !/^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$/.test(rc.sm2.nextReviewDate)) {
   156→      throw new Error(`Invalid SM2 state for card ${rc.card.id}: bad nextReviewDate format`);
   157→    }
   158→  }
   159→}
   160→```
   161→
   162→Validation is lightweight (checks required fields, types, and date format) to catch corruption without being overly strict.
   163→
   164→## Function Signatures
   165→
   166→### `loadDeck`
   167→
   168→```ts
   169→/** Load a deck from a JSON file. Returns empty array if file doesn't exist. */
   170→export function loadDeck(filePath: string): Promise<ReviewCard[]>;
   171→```
   172→
   173→- Uses `Bun.file(filePath)` to read
   174→- If file does not exist, returns `[]` (no error)

   190→### `addCardToDeck`

   193→/** Add a new card to a deck file. Loads, appends, saves. */

   200→### `updateCardsInDeck`

   207→- Loads deck, replaces cards matching by `card.id`, saves

   209→
   210→## DeckFile Type
   211→
   212→```ts
   213→/** The shape of the JSON file on disk. */
   214→interface DeckFile {
   215→  readonly version: number;
   216→  readonly cards: readonly ReviewCard[];
   217→}

   219→
   220→This is internal to `storage.ts` and not exported. The public API works with `ReviewCard[]`.
   221→
   222→## File I/O Details
   223→
   224→- **Read**: `const file = Bun.file(filePath); const text = await file.text(); JSON.parse(text)`
   225→- **Write**: Uses atomic write-to-temp-then-rename pattern (see below)
   226→- **File existence check**: `const file = Bun.file(filePath); const exists = await file.exists();`
   227→- All I/O is async (returns Promises)
   228→
   229→### Atomic Write Pattern
   230→
   231→All file writes use a write-to-temp-then-rename strategy to prevent corruption from crashes mid-write:
   232→
   233→```ts
   234→async function atomicWrite(filePath: string, data: string): Promise<void> {
   235→  const tempPath = filePath + ".tmp";
   236→  const bakPath = filePath + ".bak";
   237→
   238→  // 1. Write to temp file
   239→  await Bun.write(tempPath, data);
   240→
   241→  // 2. Create backup of existing file (if it exists)
   242→  const existing = Bun.file(filePath);
   243→  if (await existing.exists()) {
   244→    // Copy current file to .bak before overwriting
   245→    await Bun.write(bakPath, existing);
   246→  }
   247→
   248→  // 3. Atomically rename temp to target
   249→  const fs = await import("node:fs/promises");
   250→  await fs.rename(tempPath, filePath);
   251→}
   252→```
   253→
   254→- If the process crashes during step 1, the original file is untouched.
   255→- If the process crashes during step 3, the `.bak` file provides recovery.
   256→- `fs.rename()` is atomic on POSIX systems (same filesystem).
   257→
   258→### Backup Strategy
   259→
   260→- A `.bak` file is created before every save operation.
   261→- Recovery: if the main file is missing or corrupt, check for `<path>.bak` and offer to restore.
   262→- Only the most recent backup is kept (one `.bak` per deck file).
   263→
   264→### Review History Cap
   265→
   266→To prevent unbounded growth of `reviewHistory`, a maximum of **50** entries is retained per card. When the history exceeds this limit, the oldest entries are trimmed during save:
   267→
   268→```ts
   269→const MAX_REVIEW_HISTORY = 50;
   270→
   271→function trimHistory(history: readonly ReviewRecord[]): ReviewRecord[] {
   272→  if (history.length <= MAX_REVIEW_HISTORY) return [...history];
   273→  return history.slice(history.length - MAX_REVIEW_HISTORY);
   274→}
   275→```
   276→
   277→This is applied in `saveDeck` before writing, so loaded data is never silently mutated.
   278→
   279→### Concurrent Access Limitation
   280→
   281→**Important:** This storage layer assumes single-process access. There is no file locking mechanism. Running multiple CLI processes against the same deck file simultaneously may cause data loss due to read-modify-write race conditions. This is acceptable for a single-user CLI tool. If concurrent access is needed in the future, consider advisory file locking (e.g., lockfile) or switching to a database backend.
   282→
   283→## Error Handling
   284→
   285→| Scenario | Behavior |
   286→|----------|----------|
   287→| File does not exist | Return empty `ReviewCard[]` |
   288→| File is empty | Return empty `ReviewCard[]` |
   289→| File contains invalid JSON | Throw `Error("Failed to parse deck file: <path>. Invalid JSON.")` |
   290→| File contains valid JSON but wrong shape | Apply best-effort backward compat; log warning for unrecognized fields |
   291→| Write fails (permissions, disk full) | Let the Bun error propagate (caller handles) |
   292→
   293→## Default Deck Path
   294→
   295→```ts
   296→/** Default deck file path. */
   297→export const DEFAULT_DECK_PATH = "flashcards.json";
   298→```
   299→
   300→The CLI uses this as the default when no `--deck` flag is provided. The path is relative to the current working directory.
   301→
   302→## Testing Strategy
   303→
   304→Storage tests use real temporary files (not mocks) for high-fidelity I/O testing.
   305→
   306→**Setup/teardown:** Each test creates a temp directory, writes fixture files, and cleans up after.
   307→
   308→**Key test cases:**
   309→- `loadDeck`: file not found returns `[]`
   310→- `loadDeck`: empty file returns `[]`
   311→- `loadDeck`: invalid JSON throws descriptive error
   312→- `loadDeck`: v0 format (flat Card array) is migrated to v1 ReviewCard format
   313→- `loadDeck`: v1 format loads correctly
   314→- `loadDeck`: forward-version file (version > current) throws error
   315→- `loadDeck`: validation catches missing/invalid fields (NaN EF, bad date format)
   316→- `saveDeck`: creates file if it doesn't exist
   317→- `saveDeck`: atomic write — original file intact if write is interrupted
   318→- `saveDeck`: `.bak` file is created before overwriting
   319→- `saveDeck`: review history is trimmed to MAX_REVIEW_HISTORY
   320→- `addCardToDeck`: appends card with default SM2State
   321→- `updateCardsInDeck`: replaces matching cards by ID, leaves others unchanged
   322→- Round-trip: save then load preserves all data
   323→

     2→
     3→## Subsystem Map
     4→
     5→```
     6→src/
     7→  sm2.ts       — SM-2 algorithm core (pure functions, no I/O)
     8→  storage.ts   — JSON file persistence for decks with review data
     9→  quiz.ts      — Quiz engine with card prioritization and graded answers (modified)
    10→  score.ts     — Score calculation updated for quality-based grading (modified)
    11→  card.ts      — Card interface (unchanged)
    12→  index.ts     — CLI entry point with new flags and interactive prompts (modified)
    13→tests/
    14→  sm2.test.ts      — SM-2 algorithm tests
    15→  storage.test.ts  — Storage layer tests
    16→  quiz.test.ts     — Quiz engine tests
    17→  score.test.ts    — Score calculation tests
    18→```
    19→
    20→## Subsystem Responsibilities
    21→
    22→### 1. SM-2 Algorithm Core (`src/sm2.ts`) — NEW
    23→- Pure, stateless functions implementing the SM-2 algorithm
    24→- `createInitialSM2State()` — returns default state (EF=2.5, repetitions=0, interval=0)
    25→- `calculateSM2(state, quality)` — takes current state + grade (0-5), returns new state
    26→- `mapGradeToQuality(grade)` — maps 4-point user grade (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) to SM-2 quality (0/3/4/5)
    27→- `isDue(state, now)` — checks if a card is due for review
    28→- No dependencies on other modules; no I/O; fully testable in isolation
    29→
    30→### 2. Storage Layer (`src/storage.ts`) — NEW
    31→- Reads and writes deck JSON files containing cards with embedded SM-2 state
    32→- `loadDeck(filePath)` — reads JSON file, returns array of ReviewCards; handles missing files (returns empty)
    33→- `saveDeck(filePath, cards)` — writes ReviewCard array to JSON file (atomic write with .bak backup)
    34→- Backward compatible: cards without SM-2 fields are assigned default initial state on load
    35→- Versioned migration pipeline for schema evolution
    36→- Load-time validation of required fields and data types
    37→- Uses `Bun.file()` and `Bun.write()` for I/O
    38→
    39→### 3. Quiz Engine (`src/quiz.ts`) — MODIFIED
    40→- Card selection: filters due cards and new cards separately
    41→- Prioritization: due cards sorted by overdue-ness (most overdue first), then new cards up to daily limit
    42→- Answer recording changes from `boolean` to quality grade (`number`)
    43→- After each answer, applies SM-2 calculation and updates card state
    44→- Session tracks `ReviewCard[]` instead of `Card[]`
    45→
    46→### 4. Score Calculation (`src/score.ts`) — MODIFIED
    47→- Updated to work with quality grades instead of boolean correct/incorrect
    48→- Correct = quality >= 3 (maps to SM-2 "successful recall")
    49→- Adds session summary with next review date information
    50→
    51→### 5. CLI Integration (`src/index.ts`) — MODIFIED
    52→- Parses new flags: `--due-only`, `--new-cards <n>`, `--all`, `--help`
    53→- Interactive grading prompt: shows 4 options (Again/Hard/Good/Easy) after revealing answer
    54→- Graceful quit ('q' key) and SIGINT handler to save partial progress
    55→- Session summary output: cards reviewed, accuracy, next review dates
    56→- Auto-saves review results to deck file after quiz completes
    57→
    58→## Boundaries and Communication
    59→
    60→```
    61→CLI (index.ts)
    62→  │
    63→  ├── reads flags, orchestrates session lifecycle
    64→  │
    65→  ├──▶ Storage (storage.ts)
    66→  │      │  loadDeck() → ReviewCard[]
    67→  │      │  saveDeck(ReviewCard[])
    68→  │      │
    69→  │      └──▶ SM2 Core (sm2.ts)
    70→  │             createInitialSM2State() — used for backward compat
    71→  │
    72→  ├──▶ Quiz Engine (quiz.ts)
    73→  │      │  getDueCards(), getNewCards()
    74→  │      │  startQuiz(), answerCard(), currentCard()
    75→  │      │
    76→  │      └──▶ SM2 Core (sm2.ts)
    77→  │             calculateSM2() — called after each answer
    78→  │             mapGradeToQuality() — 4-point → SM-2 mapping
    79→  │
    80→  └──▶ Score (score.ts)
    81→         calculateScore(), formatScore()
    82→```
    83→
    84→## Data Flow
    85→
    86→1. **Load**: CLI calls `loadDeck()` which reads JSON and hydrates `ReviewCard[]`
    87→2. **Filter**: Quiz engine separates due cards from new cards, applies limits
    88→3. **Quiz loop**: For each card — show front, reveal back, prompt for grade
    89→4. **Update**: After each grade, `calculateSM2()` produces new SM2State; card is updated in-memory
    90→5. **Save**: After quiz completes, CLI calls `saveDeck()` to persist all updated states
    91→6. **Report**: Score module summarizes the session
    92→
    93→## Key Design Decisions
    94→
    95→- **SM-2 state per card (not per direction)**: Each card has one SM2State. No front/back separate tracking.
    96→- **4-point grading scale**: Again (0) / Hard (3) / Good (4) / Easy (5) mapped to SM-2 quality. Balances simplicity with expressiveness.
    97→- **Embedded SM-2 fields**: SM-2 state is stored alongside card data in the same JSON file, not in a separate database.
    98→- **No external dependencies**: SM-2 is simple math; dates use built-in `Date`; I/O uses Bun APIs.
    99→- **Dates as ISO 8601 strings**: `nextReviewDate` uses date-only format (`YYYY-MM-DD`) to avoid timezone issues.
   100→- **Composition over extension**: `ReviewCard` wraps `Card` + `SM2State` + `ReviewRecord[]` rather than adding optional fields to `Card`.
   101→

1→# Conventions
     2→
     3→## Language & Runtime
     4→- TypeScript with strict mode enabled
     5→- Bun as the runtime and build tool (not Node.js)
     6→- ESNext target and module system with bundler module resolution
     7→
     8→## Project Structure
     9→```
    10→src/           # Source modules (one concept per file)
    11→  index.ts     # CLI entry point
    12→  card.ts      # Card data model and creation
    13→  quiz.ts      # Quiz session logic
    14→  score.ts     # Score calculation and formatting
    15→tests/         # Test files mirroring src/ with .test.ts suffix
    16→dist/          # Build output (bun build)
    17→```
    18→
    19→## Code Style
    20→- Linting and formatting via Biome (recommended rules, organized imports)
    21→- `.goodplan/` directory is excluded from Biome checks
    22→- ES module syntax (`import`/`export`), no CommonJS
    23→- `type` imports used for type-only imports (e.g., `import type { Card }`)
    24→
    25→## Naming
    26→- Interfaces: PascalCase (e.g., `Card`, `QuizSession`, `ScoreSummary`)
    27→- Functions: camelCase, exported as named exports (e.g., `createCard`, `startQuiz`)
    28→- Files: lowercase, single-word names matching the primary concept they contain
    29→- No default exports -- all exports are named
    30→
    31→## Type Patterns
    32→- Interfaces prefer `readonly` properties where mutation is not needed
    33→- `readonly` arrays used for immutable collections (e.g., `readonly string[]`, `readonly Card[]`)
    34→- Mutable state is explicit (e.g., `currentIndex` in `QuizSession`)
    35→
    36→## Documentation
    37→- JSDoc single-line comments (`/** ... */`) on all exported interfaces and functions
    38→- No inline comments except for TODOs or clarifying notes
    39→
    40→## Testing
    41→- Bun's built-in test runner (`bun:test`)
    42→- Test files in `tests/` directory with `.test.ts` suffix
    43→- Tests use `describe`/`it`/`expect` pattern
    44→- Test file names mirror source file names (e.g., `card.test.ts` tests `card.ts`)
    45→
    46→## Build & Scripts
    47→- `bun build src/index.ts --outdir dist` for production build
    48→- `biome check .` for linting
    49→- `bun test` for running tests

1→# Quiz Engine — Detailed Design
     2→
     3→## File: `src/quiz.ts` (modified)
     4→
     5→## Card Prioritization Algorithm
     6→
     7→The quiz engine selects and orders cards in two tiers:
     8→
     9→### Tier 1: Due Cards
    10→Cards where `nextReviewDate <= today`. Sorted by overdue-ness (most overdue first).
    11→
    12→```ts
    13→function getDueCards(cards: readonly ReviewCard[], today?: string): ReviewCard[] {
    14→  const t = today ?? todayDateString();
    15→  return cards
    16→    .filter(rc => rc.sm2.nextReviewDate <= t)
    17→    .sort((a, b) => {
    18→      // Most overdue first (earlier nextReviewDate = more overdue)
    19→      if (a.sm2.nextReviewDate < b.sm2.nextReviewDate) return -1;
    20→      if (a.sm2.nextReviewDate > b.sm2.nextReviewDate) return 1;
    21→      // Tie-break: lower easiness factor first (harder cards)
    22→      return a.sm2.easinessFactor - b.sm2.easinessFactor;
    23→    });
    24→}
    25→```
    26→
    27→### Tier 2: New Cards
    28→Cards that have never been reviewed (`repetitions === 0` and `interval === 0`). Limited by the daily new-card limit (default: 20).
    29→
    30→```ts
    31→function getNewCards(cards: readonly ReviewCard[], limit: number): ReviewCard[] {
    32→  return cards
    33→    .filter(rc => rc.sm2.repetitions === 0 && rc.sm2.interval === 0)
    34→    .slice(0, limit);
    35→}
    36→```
    37→
    38→### Combined Selection
    39→
    40→```ts
    41→function selectQuizCards(
    42→  cards: readonly ReviewCard[],
    43→  options: { newCardLimit: number; dueOnly: boolean; all: boolean },
    44→  today?: string
    45→): ReviewCard[] {
    46→  if (options.all) {
    47→    return [...cards];  // all cards, no filtering
    48→  }
    49→
    50→  const dueCards = getDueCards(cards, today);
    51→
    52→  if (options.dueOnly) {
    53→    return dueCards;  // only due cards, no new cards
    54→  }
    55→
    56→  const newCards = getNewCards(cards, options.newCardLimit);
    57→  return [...dueCards, ...newCards];  // due first, then new
    58→}
    59→```
    60→
    61→No interleaving: all due cards are presented before any new cards.
    62→
    63→## Daily New-Card Limit
    64→
    65→- Default: 20
    66→- Configurable via `--new-cards <n>` CLI flag
    67→- Set to 0 to disable new cards entirely (equivalent to `--due-only`)
    68→- The limit applies to cards with `repetitions === 0 && interval === 0`
    69→- Note: a card that was reviewed once with "again" has `repetitions=0` but `interval=1` — it is a due card, not a new card. The new-card limit does not apply to it.
    70→
    71→## Updated QuizSession Interface
    72→
    73→```ts
    74→/** Quiz session state for spaced repetition. */
    75→export interface QuizSession {
    76→  readonly cards: readonly ReviewCard[];
    77→  currentIndex: number;
    78→  readonly answers: Map<string, number>;  // cardId -> SM-2 quality grade
    79→  readonly updatedCards: ReviewCard[];     // cards with updated SM-2 state after grading
    80→}
    81→```
    82→
    83→Key changes from current:
    84→- `cards` is `ReviewCard[]` instead of `Card[]`
    85→- `answers` maps to `number` (quality grade 0-5) instead of `boolean`
    86→- `updatedCards` accumulates cards with their new SM-2 state after each answer
    87→
    88→## Updated Function Signatures
    89→
    90→### `startQuiz`
    91→
    92→```ts
    93→/** Start a new quiz session with pre-selected ReviewCards. */
    94→export function startQuiz(cards: ReviewCard[]): QuizSession;
    95→```
    96→
    97→- Initializes session with `currentIndex: 0`, empty `answers` map, empty `updatedCards`
    98→- Card selection/filtering happens before `startQuiz` is called (in CLI layer)
    99→
   100→### `currentCard`
   101→
   102→```ts
   103→/** Get the current ReviewCard, or undefined if quiz is complete. */
   104→export function currentCard(session: QuizSession): ReviewCard | undefined;
   105→```
   106→
   107→### `answerCard`
   108→
   109→```ts
   110→/** Record a graded answer, apply SM-2 update, and advance to next card. */
   111→export function answerCard(session: QuizSession, grade: Grade): void;
   112→```
   113→
   114→**Pseudocode:**
   115→```
   116→function answerCard(session, grade):
   117→  rc = currentCard(session)
   118→  if rc is undefined: return
   119→
   120→  quality = mapGradeToQuality(grade)
   121→  newSM2 = calculateSM2(rc.sm2, quality)
   122→  reviewRecord = { quality, grade, reviewedAt: now(), easinessFactor: newSM2.easinessFactor, interval: newSM2.interval }
   123→
   124→  updatedCard = {
   125→    card: rc.card,
   126→    sm2: newSM2,
   127→    reviewHistory: [...rc.reviewHistory, reviewRecord]
   128→  }
   129→
   130→  session.answers.set(rc.card.id, quality)
   131→  session.updatedCards.push(updatedCard)
   132→  session.currentIndex++
   133→```
   134→
   135→### `isQuizComplete`
   136→
   137→```ts
   138→/** Check if the quiz is complete. */
   139→export function isQuizComplete(session: QuizSession): boolean;
   140→```
   141→
   142→Unchanged logic: `session.currentIndex >= session.cards.length`.
   143→
   144→### `getDueCards` (new export)
   145→
   146→```ts
   147→/** Get cards that are due for review, sorted by overdue-ness. */
   148→export function getDueCards(cards: readonly ReviewCard[], today?: string): ReviewCard[];
   149→```
   150→
   151→### `getNewCards` (new export)
   152→
   153→```ts
   154→/** Get cards that have never been reviewed, up to the specified limit. */
   155→export function getNewCards(cards: readonly ReviewCard[], limit: number): ReviewCard[];
   156→```
   157→
   158→### `selectQuizCards` (new export)
   159→
   160→```ts
   161→/** Select and order cards for a quiz session based on options. */
   162→export function selectQuizCards(
   163→  cards: readonly ReviewCard[],
   164→  options: QuizOptions,
   165→  today?: string
   166→): ReviewCard[];
   167→```
   168→
   169→## QuizOptions Type
   170→
   171→```ts
   172→/** Options for card selection in a quiz session. */
   173→export interface QuizOptions {
   174→  readonly newCardLimit: number;  // default 20
   175→  readonly dueOnly: boolean;     // only show due cards
   176→  readonly all: boolean;         // show all cards regardless of schedule
   177→}
   178→
   179→export const DEFAULT_QUIZ_OPTIONS: QuizOptions = {
   180→  newCardLimit: 20,
   181→  dueOnly: false,
   182→  all: false,
   183→};
   184→```
   185→
   186→## 4-Point Grading Flow
   187→
   188→During a quiz session, for each card:
   189→
   190→1. Display card front (question)
   191→2. User presses Enter to reveal answer
   192→3. Display card back (answer)
   193→4. Prompt: `Rate your recall: (1) Again / (2) Hard / (3) Good / (4) Easy / (q) Quit`
   194→5. User enters `1`, `2`, `3`, `4`, or `q`
   195→6. Grade is mapped to SM-2 quality and applied
   196→7. Advance to next card
   197→
   198→The grading prompt accepts single-character input for speed.
   199→
   200→## Session Lifecycle
   201→
   202→```
   203→1. Load deck from file          → ReviewCard[]
   204→2. Select quiz cards            → ReviewCard[] (filtered + sorted)
   205→3. Start quiz session           → QuizSession
   206→4. Loop: show card, grade       → updates QuizSession.updatedCards
   207→5. Quiz complete                → QuizSession with all updatedCards
   208→6. Calculate score              → ScoreSummary
   209→7. Merge updatedCards into deck → full ReviewCard[] with updates applied
   210→8. Save deck to file            → persist to disk
   211→9. Display session summary      → print to console
   212→```
   213→
   214→Step 7 detail: the CLI merges `session.updatedCards` back into the full deck array by matching on `card.id`, then saves the complete deck.
   215→
   216→## Empty State Handling
   217→
   218→| Scenario | Behavior |
   219→|----------|----------|
   220→| Deck file doesn't exist | Print "No deck found. Create cards first." and exit |
   221→| Deck exists but empty | Print "Deck is empty. Add cards first." and exit |
   222→| No due cards and `--due-only` | Print "No cards due for review. Great job!" and exit |
   223→| No due cards and no new cards | Print "No cards due. All caught up!" and exit |
   224→| Some due, some new | Show due cards first, then new cards up to limit |
   225→
   226→## Score Calculation Updates
   227→
   228→`src/score.ts` is updated to accept quality-based answers:
   229→
   230→```ts
   231→/** Calculate score from quality-grade answers. Quality >= 3 counts as correct. */
   232→export function calculateScore(answers: Map<string, number>): ScoreSummary;
   233→```
   234→
   235→The `ScoreSummary` interface remains the same. A quality of 3, 4, or 5 counts as "recalled"; 0, 1, or 2 counts as "incorrect".
   236→
   237→## Testing Strategy
   238→
   239→**Unit tests for card selection:**
   240→- `getDueCards`: returns only cards with nextReviewDate <= today, sorted by overdue-ness
   241→- `getDueCards`: tie-breaking by lower EF (harder cards first)
   242→- `getNewCards`: returns only never-reviewed cards, respects limit
   243→- `selectQuizCards`: `--all` returns all cards
   244→- `selectQuizCards`: `--due-only` excludes new cards
   245→- `selectQuizCards`: default returns due + new (up to limit), due first
   246→
   247→**Unit tests for session lifecycle:**

   249→- `answerCard`: applies SM-2 calculation and pushes to updatedCards
   250→- `answerCard`: records correct quality in answers map
   251→- `isQuizComplete`: true when currentIndex >= cards.length
   252→- `currentCard`: returns undefined when quiz complete
   253→
   254→**Integration test scenarios:**

   256→- Mixed grades: verify each grade produces expected SM2 state changes
   257→- Card with "again" grade reviewed again appears as due card (not new card)

    59→
    60→```
    61→CLI (index.ts)
    62→  │
    63→  ├── reads flags, orchestrates session lifecycle
    64→  │
    65→  ├──▶ Storage (storage.ts)
    66→  │      │  loadDeck() → ReviewCard[]
    67→  │      │  saveDeck(ReviewCard[])
    68→  │      │
    69→  │      └──▶ SM2 Core (sm2.ts)
    70→  │             createInitialSM2State() — used for backward compat
    71→  │
    72→  ├──▶ Quiz Engine (quiz.ts)
    73→  │      │  getDueCards(), getNewCards()
    74→  │      │  startQuiz(), answerCard(), currentCard()
    75→  │      │
    76→  │      └──▶ SM2 Core (sm2.ts)
    77→  │             calculateSM2() — called after each answer
    78→  │             mapGradeToQuality() — 4-point → SM-2 mapping
    79→  │
    80→  └──▶ Score (score.ts)
    81→         calculateScore(), formatScore()
    82→```
    83→
    84→## Data Flow
    85→
    86→1. **Load**: CLI calls `loadDeck()` which reads JSON and hydrates `ReviewCard[]`
    87→2. **Filter**: Quiz engine separates due cards from new cards, applies limits
    88→3. **Quiz loop**: For each card — show front, reveal back, prompt for grade
    89→4. **Update**: After each grade, `calculateSM2()` produces new SM2State; card is updated in-memory
    90→5. **Save**: After quiz completes, CLI calls `saveDeck()` to persist all updated states
    91→6. **Report**: Score module summarizes the session
    92→
    93→## Key Design Decisions
    94→
    95→- **SM-2 state per card (not per direction)**: Each card has one SM2State. No front/back separate tracking.
    96→- **4-point grading scale**: Again (0) / Hard (3) / Good (4) / Easy (5) mapped to SM-2 quality. Balances simplicity with expressiveness.
    97→- **Embedded SM-2 fields**: SM-2 state is stored alongside card data in the same JSON file, not in a separate database.
    98→- **No external dependencies**: SM-2 is simple math; dates use built-in `Date`; I/O uses Bun APIs.
    99→- **Dates as ISO 8601 strings**: `nextReviewDate` uses date-only format (`YYYY-MM-DD`) to avoid timezone issues.
   100→- **Composition over extension**: `ReviewCard` wraps `Card` + `SM2State` + `ReviewRecord[]` rather than adding optional fields to `Card`.

1→# SM-2 Algorithm Core — Detailed Design
     2→
     3→## File: `src/sm2.ts`
     4→
     5→## Types
     6→
     7→```ts
     8→/** SM-2 quality grade: integer 0-5 for compile-time safety. */
     9→export type SM2Quality = 0 | 1 | 2 | 3 | 4 | 5;
    10→
    11→/** SM-2 state tracked per card. */
    12→export interface SM2State {
    13→  readonly easinessFactor: number;   // >= 1.3, default 2.5
    14→  readonly repetitions: number;      // consecutive correct count, resets on failure
    15→  readonly interval: number;         // days until next review
    16→  readonly nextReviewDate: string;   // ISO 8601 date-only string (YYYY-MM-DD)
    17→}
    18→
    19→/** Record of a single review event. */
    20→export interface ReviewRecord {
    21→  readonly quality: SM2Quality;      // SM-2 quality grade (0-5) that was applied
    22→  readonly grade: Grade;             // user-facing grade that was given
    23→  readonly reviewedAt: string;       // ISO 8601 datetime string
    24→  readonly easinessFactor: number;   // EF after this review
    25→  readonly interval: number;         // interval after this review
    26→}
    27→
    28→/** 4-point user-facing grade scale. */
    29→export type Grade = "again" | "hard" | "good" | "easy";
    30→```
    31→
    32→## Constants
    33→
    34→```ts
    35→const INITIAL_EASINESS_FACTOR = 2.5;
    36→const MINIMUM_EASINESS_FACTOR = 1.3;
    37→const INITIAL_REPETITIONS = 0;
    38→const INITIAL_INTERVAL = 0;
    39→
    40→/** Mapping from user-facing grade to SM-2 quality (0-5). */
    41→const GRADE_TO_QUALITY: Record<Grade, SM2Quality> = {
    42→  again: 0,  // complete failure — resets repetitions
    43→  hard: 3,   // correct but with serious difficulty
    44→  good: 4,   // correct with some hesitation
    45→  easy: 5,   // perfect recall
    46→};
    47→```
    48→
    49→## Function Signatures
    50→
    51→### `createInitialSM2State`
    52→
    53→```ts
    54→/** Create the default SM-2 state for a new card. */
    55→export function createInitialSM2State(today?: string): SM2State;
    56→```
    57→
    58→- Returns `{ easinessFactor: 2.5, repetitions: 0, interval: 0, nextReviewDate: today }`
    59→- `today` defaults to current date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format if not provided
    60→- A card with initial state is immediately due for review
    61→
    62→### `calculateSM2`
    63→
    64→```ts
    65→/** Apply one review to an SM-2 state, returning the updated state. Pure function. */
    66→export function calculateSM2(state: SM2State, quality: SM2Quality, today?: string): SM2State;
    67→```
    68→
    69→- `quality` must be an integer 0-5 (validated; throws if out of range)
    70→- `today` defaults to current date in `YYYY-MM-DD` format
    71→
    72→**Algorithm pseudocode:**
    73→
    74→```
    75→function calculateSM2(state, quality, today):
    76→  // Step 1: Determine interval and repetitions (using CURRENT EF)
    77→  if quality >= 3:
    78→    if state.repetitions === 0:
    79→      newInterval = 1
    80→    else if state.repetitions === 1:
    81→      newInterval = 6
    82→    else:
    83→      newInterval = round(state.interval * state.easinessFactor)
    84→    newInterval = max(newInterval, 1)   // safety guard
    85→    newRepetitions = state.repetitions + 1
    86→  else:
    87→    // Failed recall — reset
    88→    newInterval = 1
    89→    newRepetitions = 0
    90→
    91→  // Step 2: Update easiness factor (AFTER interval calculation)
    92→  newEF = state.easinessFactor + (0.1 - (5 - quality) * (0.08 + (5 - quality) * 0.02))
    93→  newEF = max(newEF, 1.3)
    94→
    95→  // Step 3: Calculate next review date
    96→  nextReviewDate = addDays(today, newInterval)
    97→
    98→  return { easinessFactor: newEF, repetitions: newRepetitions, interval: newInterval, nextReviewDate }
    99→```

   145→

   147→- Uses `new Date()` arithmetic
   148→
   149→## Grade Mapping Rationale
   150→
   151→The full SM-2 scale (0-5) has 6 options which is too many for a CLI prompt. The 4-point scale provides a good balance between simplicity and expressiveness:
   152→
   153→| User Grade | SM-2 Quality | Meaning | SM-2 Effect |
   154→|-----------|-------------|---------|-------------|
   155→| Again (1) | 0 | No recall / wrong | Reset repetitions to 0, interval to 1 day |
   156→| Hard (2) | 3 | Recalled with difficulty | Increment repetitions, EF decreases |
   157→| Good (3) | 4 | Correct with some hesitation | Increment repetitions, EF stays ~same |
   158→| Easy (4) | 5 | Perfect recall | Increment repetitions, EF increases |
   159→
   160→Key bindings use `1/2/3/4` for speed and intuitiveness (worst to best).
   161→
   162→## Edge Cases
   163→
   164→1. **Quality validation**: `calculateSM2` throws `RangeError` if quality is not an integer 0-5
   165→2. **EF floor**: Easiness factor never drops below 1.3, even with repeated "again" grades
   166→3. **First review**: When `repetitions === 0` and quality >= 3, interval becomes 1 day (not 0)
   167→4. **Interval rounding**: `Math.round()` is used for interval calculation (SM-2 spec)
   168→5. **Date-only strings**: All dates are `YYYY-MM-DD` — no time component, no timezone ambiguity
   169→6. **Negative interval**: Not possible given the algorithm, but `Math.max(newInterval, 1)` as a safety guard
   170→
   171→## EF Progression Examples
   172→
   173→Starting from EF=2.5:
   174→- After quality=5: EF = 2.5 + 0.1 = 2.6
   175→- After quality=3: EF = 2.5 + 0.1 - 0.16 - 0.08 = 2.36
   176→- After quality=0: EF = 2.5 + 0.1 - 0.4 - 0.5 = 1.7
   177→- After quality=0 again from 1.7: EF = 1.7 + 0.1 - 0.4 - 0.5 = 0.9 → clamped to 1.3
   178→
   179→## Interval Progression (all Easy, EF=2.5)
   180→
   181→| Review # | Repetitions | Interval | Next Review |
   182→|----------|------------|----------|-------------|
   183→| 1st | 0 → 1 | 1 day | tomorrow |
   184→| 2nd | 1 → 2 | 6 days | +6 days |
   185→| 3rd | 2 → 3 | round(6 * 2.5) = 15 days | +15 days |
   186→| 4th | 3 → 4 | round(15 * 2.6) = 39 days | +39 days |
   187→
   188→## Testing Strategy
   189→
   190→All SM-2 functions are pure (no I/O, no side effects), making them ideal for unit testing.
   191→
   192→**Key test cases for `calculateSM2`:**
   193→- Quality >= 3 with repetitions=0 produces interval=1
   194→- Quality >= 3 with repetitions=1 produces interval=6
   195→- Quality >= 3 with repetitions>=2 uses `interval * oldEF` (verify old EF is used, not new)
   196→- Quality < 3 resets repetitions to 0 and interval to 1
   197→- EF never drops below 1.3 (test with repeated low-quality grades)
   198→- EF increases with quality=5, decreases with quality=3, stays roughly same with quality=4
   199→- Interval is always >= 1 (safety guard)
   200→
   201→**Key test cases for `mapGradeToQuality`:**
   202→- Each grade maps to the expected quality value
   203→- Return type is `SM2Quality`
   204→
   205→**Key test cases for `isDue` / `getOverdueDays`:**
   206→- Card due today returns true / 0 days overdue
   207→- Card due yesterday returns true / 1 day overdue
   208→- Card due tomorrow returns false / 0 days overdue
   209→
   210→**Key test cases for `createInitialSM2State`:**
   211→- Default values: EF=2.5, repetitions=0, interval=0
   212→- nextReviewDate matches provided or current date
